transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-09-23
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 mins
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Marcus Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Kumar (DataNova ML Eng), Carlos Mendes (DataNova Platform), Aisha Rahman (CTO)
Links shared: benchmark sheet https://redwood.example/benchmarks/CRM-20482, config gist https://gist.github.com/redwood/batching-config

Summary: quick squeeze test results from last week, discussion of continuous batching parameters, concurrency targets, queueing/backpressure strategy, and next steps to run an extended soak and tighten cost estimates. Customer still evaluating hosted vs dedicated; security and VPC details need follow-up.

Topics:
- Soak test numbers and patterns
- Batching window and max tokens per batch tuning
- Concurrency targets and autoscaler behavior
- Queueing/backpressure and fallbacks
- Cost tradeoffs (latency vs QPS/cost)

Action items (as read out): Marcus to run longer soak, Priya to share traffic profile, Lena to send tuned config and cost delta table.

Transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: All right thanks everyone for joining, we'll keep this tight 45 minutes, quick recap from last week and then dive into the throughput numbers. Marcus do you want to start with the soak results?
[00:18] Marcus Chen: Yeah sure, so we ran the 1-hour soak at 120 QPS on the dev cluster, used the batching window of 20 ms and max batch tokens 2048, we saw average latency around 220 ms P50, P95 was around 780 ms and there was a tail at P99 about 1.6s. The cost per 1k tokens was roughly in line with the estimate, but we hit some queueing when concurrency spiked.
[00:42] Priya Kumar: Right, the spike was during the morning ramp where we had a lot of short requests, like 16-64 tokens, and then a few long ones. We were trying to mimic prod pattern but maybe our seq length mix is off, I'll upload the histogram.
[01:05] Carlos Mendes: Quick question on the KV cache, I think in the run it wasn't enabled for some of the sequences? I saw mention of "KV cash" in the logs, not sure what that is.
[01:18] Marcus Chen: Yeah sorry auto-transcribe, KV cache was mostly enabled, we found evictions on long context runs which reduced hit rate; that bumped up compute for repeated prefixes. We can increase per-worker KV capacity or tune the cache TTL to help.
[01:37] Aisha Rahman: On dedicated versus hosted, we need to see predictable throughput — the tail behavior is a big concern for user-facing latency. We also want cost numbers if we pin dedicated capacity with burst.
[01:52] Lena Ortiz: Totally, for dedicated you get reserved GPU pools and more predictable throughput; hosted can be cheaper at low volume but you'll see some more variability. For this POC we're focused on throughput tuning so we can show you what each mode would look like in numbers.
[02:10] Priya Kumar: When you say "batching window 20 ms" what happens when there's a steady stream of requests? Do we still cap batch size?
[02:22] Marcus Chen: Good question. The runtime uses a continuous batching loop: it waits up to the batching window for more requests, but also caps by max tokens per batch and max batch size. Under steady stream you'll hit the token cap sooner and batches flush earlier, which keeps latency stable.
[02:40] Priya Kumar: Is that the same across GPU types? We run on both A100 and some T4s for inference right now.
[02:49] Marcus Chen: Kernel characteristics differ, but the batching behavior is the same. On T4 you might prefer smaller max batch tokens and lower concurrency targets because of lower memory. On A100 we can push bigger batches and more concurrency.
[03:03] Carlos Mendes: About backpressure — when queue fills how does Redwood handle it? Do we drop or reject?
[03:12] Lena Ortiz: We expose configurable queue limits and a grace policy: you can either start returning 429s when the queue is full, or apply a soft-shed where older low-priority requests are deprioritized. We can also route overflow to a cheaper model variant for degradation.
[03:26] Priya Kumar: That routing sounds interesting — could we route short chat queries to a smaller quantized variant?
[03:32] Marcus Chen: Yes, that's a common pattern. We tested a fallback to a 4-bit quantized variant for short interactions — cost dropped by ~40% but the quality delta was minimal on our eval prompts. We'll include the eval artifacts in the sheet.
[03:50] Aisha Rahman: I want to flag compliance: any config that writes logs to third-party analytics needs to be vetted. Are audit logs and KMS already in the roadmap for Private deployment?
[04:02] Lena Ortiz: Yep Private offers KMS/HSM integration and audit logs, and we can scope a security review. That's one of the next steps.
[04:12] Marcus Chen: Back to the numbers — during the hour-long soak we saw CPU-bound latencies on the worker host when concurrency > 24, that caused the dispatcher to queue requests which ballooned P95. Reducing concurrency to 16 fixed the host CPU contention, but throughput dropped a bit.
[04:33] Priya Kumar: Do you have recommendations for target concurrency per GPU?
[04:38] Marcus Chen: Rough guidelines: for A100 80GB with our model variant, start with concurrency 12-16, push to 20 only if batch size keeps CPU steady; for 40GB A100 maybe 8-12; for T4 it's more like 4-8. It's model and perf-profile dependent.
[04:56] Carlos Mendes: That makes sense. Can we automate the autoscaler to adjust concurrency based on CPU and batch fill rate?
[05:03] Marcus Chen: Yes we suggest autoscaler rules: target avg batch fill > 60% and CPU < 70% per worker, scale up nodes if fill drops under 40% or latency climbs above threshold. We can share the rule templates.
[05:18] Priya Kumar: About continuous batching window — what tradeoffs if we increase it to 40-60 ms?
[05:24] Marcus Chen: Increasing the window increases chances of larger batches hence better token throughput and lower cost per token, but adds base latency (twice the window worst-case if a singleton arrives at window start). For chat endpoints with strict latency SLOs we keep it lower, for high-throughput non-interactive workloads you can relax it.
[05:44] Aisha Rahman: For our use case — user-facing chat with occasional bulk processing — maybe hybrid routes make sense. Short chat route with 15-20 ms window and a background batch route for bulk jobs with 100 ms window.
[05:57] Lena Ortiz: Exactly, Redwood routing supports per-route batching and model variants, you can separate interactive and batch routes.
[06:08] Priya Kumar: One odd artifact in the logs was a spike labeled "OOM worker restart" during the 1-hour run, not sure what caused it.
[06:16] Marcus Chen: We saw that; it was an edge case where two long-context requests coincided and the per-worker memory pressure exceeded threshold. Fixes: cap per-request tokens, enforce pre-flight token checks, or scale worker memory.
[06:30] Carlos Mendes: Is that where quantization helps? If we move to lower-bit quant we reduce memory footprint?
[06:36] Marcus Chen: Yes 4-bit quantization removed about 40% of memory in our tests and reduced OOMs, but you must evaluate quality for long context tasks.
[06:46] Priya Kumar: Could the runtime perform automatic quantized fallback per request? Like if memory pressure is high, flip to quantized model?
[06:54] Marcus Chen: We have routing fallback but switching variants mid-inference is tricky. You can route subsequent requests to quantized variant during high load, or use multi-model worker pools.
[07:07] Lena Ortiz: Let's talk about the cost table — Marcus, can you summarize what changing batching window from 20 ms to 60 ms did to cost in last run?
[07:16] Marcus Chen: Sure rough numbers from the microbenchmarks: 20 ms window cost baseline X, 60 ms window lowers cost per 1k tokens by ~18% on A100 due to better batch fill. P50 latency increased around 40 ms. I'll put a delta table in the sheet.
[07:32] Priya Kumar: For SLOs we're targeting P95 < 800ms. The 1-hour soak had P95 780ms which is close but the P99 tail is concerning.
[07:42] Marcus Chen: For tail reduction we recommend combining KV cache tuning to reduce repeated token compute, CPU/process pinning to avoid host jitter, and prioritize small requests in the dispatcher to avoid head-of-line blocking.
[07:56] Carlos Mendes: About head-of-line blocking, can we use priority queues per route?
[08:01] Marcus Chen: Yes, we support priority queueing; you can set per-route priorities and max wait times. That prevents a long request from sitting in front of many short ones.
[08:12] Priya Kumar: Great. Also curious about the "continuous batching" implementation — is it single-threaded per GPU or multi-threaded?
[08:20] Marcus Chen: The scheduler is multi-threaded at the host level; per-GPU execution is single threaded in the runtime but with efficient kernel scheduling. The batching loop runs in the host scheduler and assembles tensors before sending to GPU.
[08:35] Aisha Rahman: From procurement lens, can we get an estimate of committed pricing if we reserve dedicated capacity for steady-state throughput of 120 QPS?
[08:45] Lena Ortiz: We can draft a committed capacity estimate. For reserved monthly commit we give a 20-30% discount versus on-demand hosted usage depending on term and capacity. We'll share a model.
[08:58] Priya Kumar: One operational ask: can you annotate the benchmark spreadsheet with per-run config (concurrency, batch window, token cap) so we can reproduce?
[09:04] Marcus Chen: Yes we'll add a reproducibility section per run and attach logs.
[09:10] Priya Kumar: Also please include the raw pprof-ish traces for the host so our infra team can inspect CPU spikes.
[09:15] Marcus Chen: Will do.
[09:18] Aisha Rahman: If we move to Private in future, how does autoscale work in on-prem?
[09:24] Lena Ortiz: Private supports the same autoscaler primitives; you manage node pools. For air-gapped we ship a controller that talks to the private control plane. We can workshop the on-prem autoscale model if you're interested.
[09:36] Carlos Mendes: Back to next soak — what exact config should we run?
[09:40] Marcus Chen: Proposed soak: 2 hours at 200 QPS, batch window 40 ms, max tokens per batch 4096, concurrency target 16 on A100, enable KV cache TTL increase and quantized fallback for short routes. We'll collect P50/P95/P99, CPU/mem, and batch fill rates.
[10:00] Priya Kumar: Sounds good. I'll try to run it on our staging cluster Tuesday morning and share the traffic histogram plus any infra limits.
[10:08] Lena Ortiz: Awesome. Recap of action items now: Marcus to run soak and upload results by 2027-09-25, Priya to share traffic hist by 2027-09-28, Lena to send config and cost delta by tomorrow 2027-09-24, and we'll schedule security follow-up for next week.
[10:26] Aisha Rahman: And include any notes about audit logging/KMS plans.
[10:30] Lena Ortiz: Will do. Anything else?
[10:34] Priya Kumar: One last Q — any recommended observability keys we should add?
[10:38] Marcus Chen: Track batch_fill_rate, queue_length, per-request tokens, kv_cache_hit_rate, worker_cpu_pct, and per-route latency histograms. We'll add a dashboard template.
[10:52] Lena Ortiz: Great thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the sheet and schedule.

End of call.
